text:
alex: quick follow-up from the kernel/attention rollout RFC — want to lock down the runtime flag semantics before the canary tomorrow

mira: +1, what's the current plan for per-model enablement? do we gate by model-id or model-family?

alex: intent was model-id for safety (so customer can opt exact variant), with a model-family fallback policy. schematic: enable(flags) -> model-id check -> kernel selection -> if unsupported fallback to family variant

sam: small note: runtime currently exposes two flag layers: global feature flags and model annotations. we need clear precedence docs, otherwise console + API races will confuse SREs

jess: we should also add an emergency-disable that bypasses graceful fallback and forces the runtime to use the stable kernel. useful for incidents where new kernels regress generation quality

alex: agreed. propose flag names: runtime.kernels.enable.<kernel_name> (global), runtime.kernels.model_override.<model_id> (per-model), runtime.kernels.emergency_disable (global kill-switch)

mira: can we make the per-model override support a list with priority? e.g. [kernel-v2, kernel-v1] so we can phase rollbacks without changing configs a lot

sam: that would help. also we need to store last-successful-kernel metadata in the model manifest so rollbacks can pick a known-good candidate automatically

infra-bot: deployment queued: rollout-control-service v0.19.1 -> canary on infra-canary-2 at 2026-03-21T14:50:00Z

alex: FYI the runtime will attempt KV-cache-compatible fallbacks. if a kernel isn't compatible with existing prefix cache we try a full-reset fallback path and emit metric kernel.fallback.cache_reset_count

mira: important — what's the SLO for fallback latency? we need to make sure callers see a bounded slow-path

alex: target is +200ms p95 for cache-reset fallback, otherwise we will fail fast and surface 503. that's in the rollout playbook

jess: doc request: can someone add snippets for flagging via console + API in the runbook? engineers keep asking where to flip per-model flags during trials

sam: I'll add examples. rough: API payload for per-model override:

```
PATCH /api/v1/flags/models/{model_id}
{
  "kernel_priority": ["kernel-v2-q8", "kernel-v1-fp16"]
}
```

alex: post-RFC tracking items (short):
- add precedence matrix and examples in RFC follow-up
- implement model manifest field for last-successful-kernel
- add emergency_disable boolean + telemetry for kills
- console UX for per-model lists + validation
- canary observability: kernel selection histogram + fallback_rate

mira: +1 on observability. also add a lint that prevents shipping model manifests without kernel compatibility metadata

jess: can we add a small runbook section: when to opt for family-level fallback vs per-model override? product wants decision rules

alex: yes — draft rule: prefer per-model override for customer-requested pinning / safety, prefer family fallback for performance-driven rollouts. I'll write a 2-paragraph rationale

infra-bot: canary result: rollout-control-service v0.19.1 passed health checks on infra-canary-2, metric kernel.fallback.cache_reset_count = 0, kernel_selection.success_rate = 99.7%

sam: looks good. I'll cut the PR for the manifest field and the API example now

mira: thanks all — let's rendezvous 30m before prod rollout to validate the emergency-disable path

alex: noted. tagging @jess to coordinate docs update :thumbsup:
